lines.text: Fifteen little squares make a staircase. Lots of kids say fifteen rectangles.
lines.caption: Fifteen little squares make a staircase. Lots of kids say fifteen rectangles.

lines.text: But the real answer is way BIGGER!
lines.caption: But the real answer is way BIGGER!

lines.text: How many rectangles of any size are in the stairs? Squares count too.
lines.caption: How many rectangles of any size are in the stairs? Squares count too.

lines.text: Every rectangle is set by two squares: its top-right, and its bottom-left.
lines.caption: Every rectangle is set by two squares: its top-right, and its bottom-left.

lines.text: Take the top-right square in column three, row two.
lines.caption: Take the top-right square in column three, row two.

lines.text: The bottom-left can be anywhere in this block: three times two, so six rectangles!
lines.caption: The bottom-left can be anywhere in this block: three times two, so six rectangles!

lines.text: So write column times row in every square, and add each column.
lines.caption: So write column times row in every square, and add each column.

lines.text: Why does the trick work? The full lesson shows two ways, plus every trap.
lines.caption: Why does the trick work? The full lesson shows two ways, plus every trap.
